claim: Coverage exclusion is skipped for netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework, so the requirement that all generated code carries the attribute is not met there. The templates wrap every attribute in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. That guard is unnecessary: `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in .NET Framework 4.0+ and in netstandard2.0, and it can target classes. Projects on those targets, which includes most multi-targeted libraries, get no coverage exclusion. The README also says the attribute is not available on those targets, which is false. The derived criterion only allows conditional emission where the attribute does not exist.

Those are exactly the users who care about coverage. This violates the derived criterion that generated code still compiles.
